title: QAOA and Max-Cut
summary: Combinatorial optimization on a graph, with p = 2 layers.
mission: Split the 5 vertices of the graph into two groups, cutting as many edges as possible: build the QAOA with cost layers (IsingZZ on the edges) and mixer layers (RX on every qubit) and optimize the angles until the approximation ratio exceeds 0.85.

prediction.question: With a single layer (p = 1) and the best possible angles, does the approximation ratio of this graph exceed 0.85?
options: Yes, one layer is always enough
prediction.explanation: With p = 1, the best QAOA can achieve on this graph is about 0.82. Each extra layer adds two angles and brings the state closer to the solution; with p = 2 the ratio exceeds 0.9.

hints: In the function layer(gamma, beta): for each edge (i, j) in edges, qml.IsingZZ(gamma, wires=[i, j]); then, for each qubit, qml.RX(2 * beta, wires=qubit).
The circuit starts with a Hadamard on the 5 qubits and applies one layer for each pair (gamma, beta) in params. It returns qml.expval(cost_h), which the optimizer minimizes.
Use params of shape (2, 2), that is, p = 2 layers, and optimizer = qml.AdamOptimizer(0.1) for about 80 steps, storing circuit(params) in history.
